## What to do

Adapt the upstream custom providers doc (tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/docs/custom-provider.md, 637 lines) for our Elixir system.

## Upstream source

- tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/docs/custom-provider.md
- tmp/pi-mono/packages/ai/src/providers/ (all provider implementations)
- Examples: tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/custom-provider-anthropic/
- Examples: tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/custom-provider-gitlab-duo/
- Examples: tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/custom-provider-qwen-cli/

## Output

Create docs/custom-providers.md

## How to adapt

This is a LONG doc (637 lines). Break it into sections:

1. **Quick Reference**: Convert the TypeScript `pi.registerProvider()` call to our Elixir extension API. Show how to register a provider from an extension:
   ```elixir
   # In an extension:
   def handle_event(:session_start, _ctx, host) do
     host.register_provider(%OctoPi.AI.ProviderConfig{
       name: :my_provider,
       base_url: "https://api.example.com",
       api: :openai_completions,
       api_key: "MY_API_KEY",
       models: [
         %OctoPi.AI.Model{
           id: "my-model",
           name: "My Model",
           reasoning: false,
           input: [:text],
           cost: %{input: 0, output: 0, cache_read: 0, cache_write: 0},
           context_window: 128000,
           max_tokens: 4096
         }
       ]
     })
   end
   ```

2. **Override Existing Provider**: Show how to override via extension:
   ```elixir
   host.register_provider(%ProviderConfig{
     name: :anthropic,
     base_url: "https://proxy.example.com"
   })
   ```

3. **Register New Provider**: Show the async extension factory pattern in Elixir.

4. **Unregister Provider**: Document `host.unregister_provider(:my_provider)`.

5. **API Types**: Convert the TypeScript API type enum to our Elixir atoms:
   - `:anthropic_messages`
   - `:openai_completions`
   - `:openai_responses`
   - `:azure_openai_responses`
   - `:openai_codex_responses`
   - `:mistral_conversations`
   - `:google_generative_ai`
   - `:google_gemini_cli`
   - `:google_vertex`
   - `:bedrock_converse_stream`

6. **Auth Header**: Document `auth_header: true` option.

7. **OAuth Support**: Convert the OAuth interface to our Elixir equivalent. Show our `OctoPi.AI.Auth.OAuth` module.

8. **Custom Streaming API**: Convert the TypeScript stream pattern to our Elixir Producer pattern. Show how to implement a custom provider using `OctoPi.AI.Producer`.

## What to preserve verbatim

- The API type table
- The compat flags table
- The OAuth flow concepts (PKCE, device code, prompt)
- The event types for streaming (text_start, text_delta, etc.)

## Key upstream references to include

- [anthropic.ts](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts)
- [openai-completions.ts](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts)
- [mistral.ts](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/ai/src/providers/mistral.ts)
- [google.ts](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/ai/src/providers/google.ts)
- [amazon-bedrock.ts](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/blob/main/packages/ai/src/providers/amazon-bedrock.ts)

## Testing the doc

After writing, verify:
1. All Elixir module names are correct
2. All atoms match our actual API type values
3. The OAuth flow matches our implementation
4. The Producer pattern matches our actual API
